Transfer to Guatemala City airport for a domestic flight to Flores. An English-speaking guide will accompany you.

Overnight at Villa Maya. Meals: breakfast.
Guatemala City skyline with high-rise buildings and leafy neighbourhoods
Guatemala City: high-rises among leafy neighbourhoods

Visit Tikal with an English-speaking guide. The site is about 64 km from Flores, the capital of Petén, which sits on an island in Lake Petén Itzá.

The name Tikal is translated as ‘the place where the voices of spirits can be heard’. Tikal is considered the largest settlement in pre-Columbian America. The city was inhabited from around 800 BC to AD 900, after which the jungle gradually reclaimed it. Restoration began after the site was rediscovered in the early 20th century.

The centre of Tikal covered about 16 km², excluding the outskirts, and contained some 3,000 structures. Six pyramid temples stand out. Their height and the density of the buildings led archaeologists to compare Tikal to the New York of the Maya civilisation.

Tikal National Park covers 575 km². In 1979, UNESCO added it to the World Heritage List for both its cultural and natural significance.

In the afternoon, transfer to Flores airport for a domestic flight to Guatemala City.

Overnight at Barceló Guatemala City. Meals: breakfast.
